claims.text: The proposed alloy contains approximately 40 at% Ti, 40 at% Ni, and 20 at% additional refractory or supporting elements such as V, Cr, or Al.
A composition containing approximately 40 at% Ti and 40 at% Ni meets the stated HEA compositional criterion of 5–35 at% per element.
The untreated alloy is an as-cast or homogenized single-phase solid solution lacking fine precipitates.
The intervention consists of solutionizing at approximately 1100°C for 1 hour and aging at approximately 600°C for 1–2 hours under an inert atmosphere.
Solutionizing at approximately 1100°C for 1 hour will homogenize the Ti–Ni-primary alloy and dissolve preexisting precipitates.
Aging the solutionized alloy at approximately 600°C for 1–2 hours will induce Ti2Ni-type precipitation.
The treatment will produce uniformly distributed, nanoscale, coherent Ti2Ni-type precipitates in the solid-solution matrix.
Two-step precipitation treatment can favor finer and more uniformly distributed precipitates than a single-step process.
Fine coherent intermetallic precipitates will hinder dislocation motion at elevated temperatures.
Precipitation strengthening will increase the elevated-temperature yield strength of the treated alloy relative to the untreated alloy.
Precipitation strengthening will improve the elevated-temperature creep resistance of the treated alloy relative to the untreated alloy.
Using an inert, oxygen-free atmosphere during treatment will minimize oxidation.
The proposed strengthening effect is expected to operate at test temperatures up to approximately 700°C.
Precipitate size, volume fraction, and distribution may vary with aging duration and temperature.
Prolonged aging or elevated-temperature exposure may cause over-aging or precipitate coarsening that diminishes strengthening.
Treated and untreated samples made through identical casting and homogenization procedures can serve as intervention and baseline groups.
TEM and XRD will be used to determine whether the proposed Ti2Ni-type precipitates and secondary phases form.

The hypothesis is falsified if treatment produces no statistically significant increase in elevated-temperature yield strength and creep resistance, or if the proposed uniformly dispersed nanoscale coherent Ti2Ni-type precipitates are not confirmed.

contradictions.description: The proposed alloy assigns approximately 40 at% each to Ti and Ni, while the same hypothesis says that every element is within the stated 5–35 at% HEA limit. Both Ti and Ni exceed that limit.
